samples.text:
The diagram shows the process of making paper from the wood. Overall, there is eight stages and it start with cutting trees and finish with cutting the paper to size.

First, softwood trees are cut down in managed forests. Then the bark is removed from the logs and the logs are cut into small chips. After that, the chips are cooked with chemicals, so the fibres are separated. This stage is called pulping. Next, the pulp is bleached to make it white.

In the fifth stage, the pulp is mixed with water and also with recycled fibre. Then the mixture is sprayed on a moving mesh and the water drain away, so a sheet is formed. After that, the sheet is pressed between rollers and it is dried over heated cylinders.

Finally, the paper is wound onto a large reels and then it is cut to size. In general, the process has many steps and the paper is made from trees and also from recycled fibre, which is added in the middle of process.
samples.why: Overview given early but basic · all eight stages described in order · mechanical sequencing (Then, After that, Next) · adequate vocabulary · several agreement and article errors that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The diagram illustrates how paper is manufactured from wood, from the felling of trees to the production of finished sheets.

Overall, there are eight stages in this linear process, which begins in the forest and ends with paper ready for use. The first two stages prepare the raw timber, the middle stages turn it into pulp, and the final stages form, dry and cut the paper.

At the start, softwood trees are cut down in the managed forests. The logs are then debarked and cut into chips, which is subsequently cooked with chemicals in order to separate the fibres, a stage which is known as pulping. This pulp is bleached to make it whiter, and then it is mixed with water and recycled fibre.

In the forming stage, the mixture is sprayed onto a moving mesh, allowing the water to drain away. The resulting sheet is pressed between rollers and dried as it passes over a set of heated cylinders. Finally, the paper is wound onto large reels before being cut to the required size, which completes the process.
samples.why: Clear overview grouping the stages · logical progression with good use of passives and sequencers · some less common vocabulary (debarked, resulting sheet) · mostly accurate with two minor slips.

samples.text:
The diagram sets out the eight stages involved in converting timber into paper.

Broadly speaking, the process falls into three phases: the preparation of the raw wood, the chemical treatment of that wood to create pulp, and the mechanical formation of the paper itself. It begins in managed forests and ends with the paper being reeled and trimmed to size. Notably, recycled fibre is introduced part-way through, so the finished product is not made from newly felled wood alone.

Initially, softwood trees are felled, after which their bark is stripped away and the logs are reduced to chips. These chips are then cooked with chemicals, a step known as pulping, which separates the wood fibres. The resulting pulp is bleached to whiten it and subsequently combined with water and recycled fibre.

At the forming stage, this mixture is sprayed onto a moving mesh, through which the water drains, leaving a damp sheet behind. The sheet is then pressed between rollers and dried over a series of heated cylinders. In the last step, the finished paper is wound onto large reels and later cut into sheets of the required dimensions.
samples.why: Insightful overview grouping the stages into three phases · every stage covered with precise sequencing · wide, accurate vocabulary (felled, stripped away, reduced to chips) · varied complex structures · error-free.
